property_summary: Only the contract owner can successfully withdraw the contract balance via withdrawAll()
Calls to withdrawAll revert when msg.sender is not the contract owner.
If the provided caller address is not this test contract, then calling c.withdrawAll() from this test contract must revert.

For any caller who is the owner and any contract balance >=1 wei, calling withdrawAll transfers the entire contract balance to the owner (leaving balance 0); the mutant that subtracts 1 wei breaks this by leaving 1 wei in the contract for some inputs.

For any nonzero contract balance and when the owner calls withdrawAll, the reference transfers the entire contract balance out (leaving address(c).balance == 0); the mutant that subtracts 1 wei leaves 1 wei in the contract for some fuzzed deposit amounts, violating this rule.

For any deposit amount >= 1 wei and when the owner calls withdrawAll, the reference contract drains its full balance (address(c).balance == 0) while the mutant that subtracts 1 wei leaves 1 wei behind, so the property is that after owner calls withdrawAll the contract balance becomes zero.

For any initial nonzero contract balance and when the owner calls withdrawAll, the reference C causes the owner's received amount equal to the prior contract balance (owner's balance increases by that amount) whereas the mutant sends exactly one wei less, so the owner's balance increase differs by 1 for some fuzzed deposit amounts.

For any caller who is the owner and for any initial contract balance B where B >= 1, calling withdrawAll always results in address(c).balance == 0 in the reference, but the mutant that subtracts 1 wei can leave address(c).balance == 1 for some B; the test asserts that after owner calls withdrawAll the contract balance is zero.

For any amount of Ether in the contract, calling withdrawAll() by the owner always decreases the contract balance by that amount (i.e., withdrawAll forwards the full contract balance to the owner); the mutant which calls withdraw(0) breaks this by leaving the contract balance unchanged for some inputs.

For any nonzero ether balance held by the contract, calling withdrawAll as owner transfers the entire contract balance to the owner (reducing address(c).balance to 0); the mutant that calls withdraw(0) leaves the contract balance unchanged for some nonzero balances, violating this rule.

For any owner-invoked withdrawAll call when the contract has a positive balance and the caller is the owner, the contract balance decreases (funds are forwarded to the owner); the mutant that calls withdraw(0) can leave the contract balance unchanged, violating this.

For any owner-invoked withdrawAll when the contract has a positive balance, the contract's balance strictly decreases (funds are forwarded to the owner); the mutant that calls withdraw(0) can leave the contract balance unchanged, violating this rule for some inputs.

If the owner calls withdrawAll after the contract has a positive balance, the call succeeds (does not revert) and results in a change to the contract's balance (i.e., address(c).balance decreases); the mutant that calls withdraw(0) still succeeds but can leave the contract balance unchanged, violating the rule for some inputs.
Only the owner can withdraw the contract's full balance to themselves (i.e., after funding, a withdraw by caller results in contract balance zero only if caller is the original owner).
When a non-owner calls withdraw(amount) the call must revert (only owner can successfully withdraw).
A non-owner external call to c.withdraw(amount) must revert (only the original owner may successfully withdraw).
A direct external call from this contract to c.withdraw(amount) by a non-owner must revert (i.e., non-owners cannot successfully call withdraw).

For any caller who is the owner and any withdrawn amount that the contract holds, calling withdraw(...) sends the funds to the msg.sender (the caller) so that address(c).balance decreases by the withdrawn amount and owner balance does not change; the mutant that sends to owner instead will not transfer funds to msg.sender when msg.sender != owner and so the post-call balances differ for some inputs.

For any caller who is owner and any withdrawal amount <= contract balance, calling withdraw(...) transfers that amount to msg.sender (so address(c).balance decreases by the amount); the mutant that sends to owner instead will leave address(c).balance unchanged when msg.sender != owner for some fuzzed caller, thus violating this rule.

For any caller who is the owner and any withdrawal amount x ≤ address(c).balance, calling withdraw(x) always reduces address(c).balance by x (because funds are sent to msg.sender); the mutant that sends to owner instead can fail this when the owner ≠ msg.sender (i.e. when msg.sender is owner this still holds) so the difference can be detected by fuzzing owner vs caller and amount.

For any caller who is NOT the contract owner and any withdrawal amount <= contract balance, when the owner calls withdraw(amount) the contract balance decreases by that amount (because funds are sent to msg.sender); the mutant that sends to owner instead will not transfer to the caller when caller != owner, so for some fuzzed caller the post-withdraw contract balance does not decrease by the amount.

For any address caller that is the contract owner and any amount x <= address(c).balance, calling withdraw(x) must transfer x out of the contract (reducing address(c).balance by x); the mutant that directs transfer to owner (instead of msg.sender) will fail this when the caller (msg.sender) is owner but owner != msg.sender cannot happen—so instead we choose a rule that the owner can call withdraw and the recipient of the transfer equals msg.sender (i.e., after withdraw the caller's balance increased by x), which the mutant breaks when owner != msg.sender by sending to owner; we implement this by having the owner be a helper contract that records received value—reference sends to msg.sender so the helper receives funds, mutant sends to owner (an EOA) so helper does not receive funds.

If the caller is the owner and sends Ether via sendMoney to any target, the target address's balance increases by exactly the sent amount (or the call reverts), i.e. no silent failures leave the contract with the Ether.
When sendMoney is invoked by the owner sending a positive value, the call either reverts or completes (does not silently succeed without indicating failure).
If a non-contract recipient causes the low-level call to fail, sendMoney must revert (so the call does not succeed against a failing recipient).

property_summary: For any target address and value, sendMoney(...) in the correct contract either forwards the funds (reducing C balance) or reverts on a failing low-level call; the mutant can silently fail to transfer funds leaving C's balance unchanged even when the call would fail — i.e., the reference never returns successfully while still holding the funds after attempting a failing external call, but the mutant may return successfully while keeping the funds.

For any callee that reverts when sent value, the reference contract's sendMoney call always reverts (does not return successfully) while the mutated contract may return successfully (silently ignoring failure); the test asserts that calling sendMoney against a reverting helper never returns ok (true) on the correct contract — a mutant that drops the require will make the call succeed (ok == true) for some fuzzed value.
Only the owner can cause the contract C to transfer ether out via sendMoney (i.e., after calling sendMoney, address(c).balance does not decrease when caller != owner).
Only the owner may successfully call sendMoney; non-owners' calls revert.

property_summary: sendMoney can only succeed when called by the contract owner (non-owners' calls revert).
If the call to c.sendMoney does not revert, then msg.sender must be the owner of c.
If the call to c.sendMoney does not revert, then msg.sender must be the owner of c.

Rule: Only the owner can successfully make c.sendMoney(...) transfer contract funds to an arbitrary target; the mutant relaxing onlyOwner allows non-owners to cause the contract balance to decrease for some inputs (attacker address and value), violating this invariant.

Invariant: Only the owner can cause C to send its balance out via sendMoney, so for any caller other than owner a sendMoney call must not decrease C's balance (it must revert or fail); the mutant removing the onlyOwner check allows a non-owner attacker helper to drain or transfer funds, violating this rule for some fuzzed target/amount.

For every caller who is not the owner, calling sendMoney(target, value, data) must not succeed in transferring contract balance (i.e., the call should revert or fail for non-owners); the mutant removing the onlyOwner check allows a non-owner helper to successfully make the contract send funds out for some fuzzed target/amount, violating this rule.
